From what moment does the athlete begin to enter the water surface?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: At the moment $t_{2}$, he begins to enter the water surface
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a graph of velocity v changing with time t. The horizontal axis is t, and the vertical axis is v; the curve starts near t=0 as an obliquely upward straight line, after passing t1 it continues to rise with the same slope, reaches a cusp at t2, and the position t2 is marked with a dashed line; after t2, the graph becomes another obliquely downward straight line, and near t3 the velocity becomes 0. Reasoning: From t=0 to t2, the v-t graph is a straight line with the same slope, indicating that after the athlete leaves the springboard and is in the air, he is acted on only by gravity, and the velocity changes with constant acceleration. At t2, an obvious turning point appears in the graph, and afterward the slope changes from positive to negative, indicating that the athlete's force state has changed, and he is acted on by water resistance and other effects and decelerates. Therefore, "begin to enter the water surface" should correspond to the moment when the force state has just changed, namely t2.
